featured.title: A Trillion Dollars Vanished From the Nasdaq in a Day. The Engineers Who Built the AI Boom Have the Most to Lose.
featured.excerpt: Tuesday's tech wreck wiped more than $1 trillion off the Nasdaq 100 as investors finally asked whether the debt-funded AI buildout can pay for itself. For Indian techies whose net worth, RSUs and job security ride on these stocks, the reckoning is personal.
featured.image_caption: The Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square, New York
featured.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian engineers at Nvidia, Google, Microsoft and Micron hold much of their compensation in the very AI stocks now in freefall — a correction that hits their RSUs, mortgages and visa-tethered job security harder than almost anyone.
featured.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Ambani Just Filed the Paperwork for India's Biggest-Ever IPO. The Company Is Jio.
news.excerpt: Reliance has lodged draft papers to list Jio Platforms in Mumbai in an offering that could raise about $4 billion and value the business near $137 billion. For a diaspora that already touches Jio through Meta and Google's stakes, it is a rare chance to own a slice of the network that rewired India.
news.image_caption: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani, whose Jio Platforms has filed for India's largest-ever IPO
news.nri_angle: The Jio IPO gives overseas Indians a rare, direct way to own the network that rewired daily life back home — the cheap data behind their video calls, the rails behind their remittances, the streaming that keeps them tied to Indian cricket and cinema — and, through the NRI investor route, the listing will be a marquee test of whether diaspora appetite for Indian assets holds up in a jittery market.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Got Its First Sovereign-AI Unicorn. The Bigger Question Is Whether It's Building Fast Enough.
news.excerpt: Bengaluru's Sarvam has raised $234 million to build AI models from scratch in India, even as a Wall Street note warns the country risks letting foreign systems power its banks, defence and public services. For a diaspora that staffs the world's AI labs, the contest over who controls the models is suddenly personal.
news.image_caption: A data-center server hall; India is racing to build sovereign AI models trained at home
news.nri_angle: Indians and people of Indian origin run or sit near the top of nearly every major AI lab in the United States — the very talent that built the frontier models India now worries about depending on — so India's sovereign-AI push is an attempt to give that diaspora a reason to build at home or for home, even as many NRIs work for the Western labs whose dominance New Delhi is trying to reduce.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Rescue Plan for 11,000 Stranded Sailors Is Now Underway in the Gulf. Many of Them Are Indian.
news.excerpt: The UN's shipping agency said on Tuesday it has begun contacting hundreds of vessels trapped behind the Strait of Hormuz to start evacuating some 11,000 seafarers, after the US-Iran ceasefire reopened a path through the waterway. For the world's largest single supplier of merchant sailors, the operation is intensely personal.
news.image_caption: An oil tanker at sea; the IMO has begun evacuating some 11,000 seafarers stranded behind the Strait of Hormuz
news.nri_angle: Indians are the single largest nationality in the global merchant marine — well over 250,000 serving seafarers — so a UN operation to evacuate the ~11,000 crew stranded behind the Strait of Hormuz is, for India's coastal communities, a story about their own sons and the remittances that sustain their families, and a reminder that Indian labour crews the ships carrying the world's oil just as visibly as it staffs Silicon Valley and the NHS.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Monsoon Is Running 43% Short, and the Government Is Drawing Up Plans for 300 Districts
news.excerpt: With rains the weakest in over a decade and the weather office warning of an El Nino-stunted season, New Delhi has put more than 300 farm districts on a contingency footing. For a diaspora bound to rural India by remittances and family land, a thin monsoon is more than a weather story — it is a livelihood story.
news.image_caption: A farmer in an Indian paddy field; the 2026 monsoon is running about 43% below average
news.nri_angle: A failing monsoon hits the diaspora indirectly but unmistakably — the families that NRIs support with over $100 billion in annual remittances are concentrated in rain-fed farming districts, so a poor harvest raises remittance demand even as food inflation pressures the rupee in which overseas Indians hold deposits and send money home, while the climate trajectory of Indian agriculture increasingly shapes the plans of diaspora families who own land back home or are weighing a return.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: For the First Time Since 1973, Congress Has Told a President to End a War. The War Is With Iran.
news.excerpt: The US Senate voted 50-48 on Tuesday to direct Donald Trump to pull American forces out of the conflict with Iran — the first time both chambers have passed such a resolution since the War Powers Act became law. It is likely symbolic. But for a diaspora that watched this war whipsaw oil prices, flights home and the safety of thousands of Indians in the Gulf, the vote is a signal worth reading.
news.image_caption: The US Senate; lawmakers voted 50-48 to direct President Trump to halt military action against Iran
news.nri_angle: The war this resolution targets reached deep into diaspora life — whipsawing oil prices and the rupee, threatening shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, leaving nearly 18,000 Indian seafarers trapped in Gulf waters and forcing the evacuation of 1,700 citizens — so a bipartisan Senate signal that Washington wants the conflict to end speaks directly to the energy security, currency stability and Gulf livelihoods that millions of Indian families abroad depend on.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Japan's New PM Makes Her First India Trip Next Week — With 50 Company Bosses and a Shopping List of Chips
news.excerpt: Sanae Takaichi's debut visit to India from July 1-3 will now be held in New Delhi after a planned summit in Guwahati was shelved over a tight schedule. Behind the venue shuffle sits a far bigger story: a Japanese business armada and an India-Japan agenda built around semiconductors, critical minerals and the movement of skilled people — all of which run straight through the diaspora.
news.image_caption: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi, who makes her first official visit to India from July 1-3
news.nri_angle: Japan, racing to build out semiconductors and advanced manufacturing while its own workforce shrinks, has been opening doors to skilled Indian engineers, technicians and care workers — so a summit that deepens India-Japan tech, talent-mobility and supply-chain ties opens a fresh destination for diaspora professionals beyond the usual US/UK/Canada/Gulf routes, while Japanese investment into Indian chip and clean-energy projects strengthens the home economy that NRIs stay tethered to through remittances and return migration.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Market Rally Just Hit a Wall. The Warning Sign Wasn't Oil — It Was the Monsoon.
news.excerpt: The Sensex tumbled 893 points and the Nifty fell 1.16% on Tuesday, snapping a seven-session rally, after a survey showed private-sector growth cooling to a three-month low and a patchy monsoon spooked investors. For diaspora investors who watch Indian equities and the rupee, it was a reminder of how fast the mood can turn.
news.image_caption: India's stock market; the Sensex fell 893 points on Tuesday, snapping a seven-session rally
news.nri_angle: NRIs hold Indian equities directly, through funds, and via the NRI deposit routes banks (and the RBI) have been pushing to shore up the rupee — so a sell-off driven by a slowing IT sector, Fed-hike fears and a weak monsoon speaks straight to diaspora portfolios, where the rupee's path determines how far remittances stretch and what Indian assets are worth in dollars.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A US Court Just Cleared the Way to Deport People From Anywhere in America — Without a Judge
news.excerpt: A divided federal appeals court has revived the Trump administration's power to fast-track deportations of undocumented immigrants found anywhere in the country, not just at the border. The two-year test at the centre of the ruling is exactly where visa overstays — a quiet but real slice of the Indian story in America — are most exposed.
news.image_caption: US immigration enforcement; a divided appeals court revived nationwide fast-track deportations
news.nri_angle: The revived policy turns on a two-year continuous-presence test enforced anywhere in the US — the exact zone where Indian visa overstays (lapsed F-1s, expired H-1Bs, overstayed visitor visas) are most exposed, making current documentation and proof of time in the country an urgent priority for anyone in or near a status gap, and reshaping the calculus for mixed-status diaspora families who can no longer count on the slow immigration-court backlog.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Isn't Just the World's Biggest Source of Skilled Migrants. Its Workers Now Out-Earn the Locals.
news.excerpt: New global talent data puts India at the very top of the skilled-migration map — the number-one source of US H-1B hires and a leading feeder for UK skilled-worker visas and EU Blue Cards. The twist that reframes the whole 'cheap labour' debate: Indian hires abroad are increasingly commanding a wage premium over comparable local workers, not a discount.
news.image_caption: The Infosys campus in India; Indian skilled migrants now out-earn locals in top destinations (Wikimedia Commons)
news.nri_angle: The finding that Indian skilled migrants out-earn local workers is a direct rebuttal to the 'cheap labour' narrative that shapes the visa rules, fee hikes and public mood diaspora families live under — and, with the Gulf, Australia and Canada now actively courting Indian talent and India itself drawing senior professionals home, it reframes the career map facing the diaspora's next generation from a one-way exit into a position of genuine leverage.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: UK-India Week Just Opened at Warwick — and the Real Action Is a Gujarat-to-West-Midlands Handshake
news.excerpt: The 10th edition of UK-India Week, the biggest event in the bilateral calendar, opened at the University of Warwick with a state-to-region pitch: a Gujarat delegation courting the West Midlands on advanced manufacturing, clean energy, life sciences and skills — a model that turns broad diplomacy into concrete, place-to-place partnerships.
news.image_caption: The University of Warwick, host of the 10th UK-India Week, where a Gujarat delegation courted the West Midlands
news.nri_angle: The West Midlands is a heartland of Britain's ~1.9 million-strong Indian community — much of it Gujarati, concentrated in Birmingham, Leicester and Coventry — so a formal Gujarat–West Midlands partnership turns the diaspora's ancestral state and adopted region into business partners, formalising the connective role Gujarati families have played in UK-India trade for generations and giving diaspora entrepreneurs a direct bridge between Gujarat's investment incentives and British innovation ecosystems.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India's Drug Regulator Just Flagged 159 Medicines as Substandard. Some Are Drugs You Take Every Day.
news.excerpt: In its latest monthly check, the Central Drugs Standard Control Organisation declared 159 samples 'Not of Standard Quality' and one outright spurious — covering common blood-pressure pills, diabetes tablets, antibiotics and vitamin supplements made by household-name companies. For a diaspora that treats India as its pharmacy, the list is a recurring uncomfortable read.
news.image_caption: A pile of medicine tablets; India's drug regulator flagged 159 drug samples as Not of Standard Quality in its latest monthly alert
news.nri_angle: Millions of NRIs treat India as their pharmacy — stocking up on blood-pressure pills, diabetes drugs, antibiotics and supplements on visits home or having relatives ship them abroad for a fraction of Western prices — so a monthly list of substandard and spurious medicines is a direct, practical health-safety concern for diaspora families and the ageing parents they manage from afar.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Adani Just Opened an Airport in the Heart of Kutch. For the Gujarati Diaspora, It's a New Door Home.
news.excerpt: The Mundra Airport in Gujarat began scheduled passenger flights on Tuesday via regional carrier Star Air — connecting the remote Kutch region directly to Mumbai, Goa and six other cities — as the Adani Group unveiled plans to invest about Rs 1 lakh crore across its airports over the next five years.
news.image_caption: A Star Air Embraer regional jet; Star Air launched the first scheduled passenger flights from Adani Mundra Airport in Gujarat
news.nri_angle: Kutch and Gujarat are the ancestral home of one of the largest, most prosperous Indian diasporas — communities in East Africa, the UK, US and Gulf with deep family, property and trade ties to the district — so a direct-flight airport at Mundra removes the awkward final leg of every trip home and strengthens the port-SEZ-airport logistics hub that NRI entrepreneurs watch closely.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: The Dream Degree Abroad Is Getting Too Expensive and Too Risky. Indian Families Are Doing the Math.
news.excerpt: A rupee that has lost more than a tenth of its value in a year, visa crackdowns from Washington to Ottawa, and a job market that no longer pays off the loan — the calculus that sent a generation of Indians to the West is breaking down, and the September intake is already shrinking.
news.image_caption: Graduates celebrate at a university commencement in South Asia. For many families, a foreign degree remains the aspiration even as costs and visa risks climb.
news.nri_angle: Sending a child to study in the West is the biggest financial bet most Indian middle-class and NRI families make, so a falling rupee, visa crackdowns and a broken post-graduation job market turn that bet into a potential debt trap — and increasingly the diaspora's relatives abroad are the co-signers and safety net when the loans outrun gig-economy earnings.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: A Doctor Who Built SpaceX's Medical Unit Is About to Become an Astronaut. His Roots Run to Kerala.
news.excerpt: Anil Menon — emergency physician, Space Force colonel and son of an Indian father and Ukrainian mother — launches July 14 aboard Soyuz MS-29 for an eight-month stay on the International Space Station, his first spaceflight and a rare diaspora milestone in human exploration.
news.image_caption: NASA astronaut Anil Menon, who launches aboard Soyuz MS-29 on July 14, 2026 for his first spaceflight
news.nri_angle: Astronauts who carry Indian heritage into orbit — from Rakesh Sharma to Kalpana Chawla to Sunita Williams — hold a special place for the diaspora, and Anil Menon adds a modern, hyphenated chapter as an Indian-and-Ukrainian-American physician-astronaut whose July 14 launch gives diaspora children another face that looks like their own reaching space.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: Two of the Main Roads to a US Green Card Just Closed for Indians — Until October at the Earliest
news.excerpt: The State Department's July Visa Bulletin marks both the EB-2 and the unreserved EB-5 categories "Unavailable" for India and pushes the EB-1 cutoff back another two months — freezing tens of thousands of high-skilled Indian professionals and investors in a queue that no longer moves until the new fiscal year begins.
news.image_caption: The U.S. Department of State in Washington, whose July 2026 Visa Bulletin marked India's EB-2 and unreserved EB-5 green-card categories "Unavailable"
news.nri_angle: Indians are the largest group trapped in the US employment green-card backlog, so EB-2 and unreserved EB-5 going 'Unavailable' until at least October freezes tens of thousands of high-skilled Indian professionals and investors — and puts the children of long-waiting applicants at greater risk of 'aging out' before the queue restarts.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: America Will Now Sell You a Faster Visa Interview for $750. India's Families Are the Obvious Market.
news.excerpt: From July 1, the State Department's six-month pilot lets B1/B2 visitor-visa applicants pay an extra $750 — four times the standard fee — to lock in an interview within 10 business days. It buys a slot, not a visa, and it does nothing to speed the background checks that follow.
news.image_caption: The U.S. Embassy in New Delhi; a State Department pilot lets B1/B2 visa applicants pay $750 for a faster interview from July 1, 2026
news.nri_angle: The B1/B2 visitor visa is how the Indian diaspora brings parents and relatives over for weddings, graduations and newborns, so a pay-$750-to-skip-the-line option is squarely aimed at NRI families — valuable if India's high-backlog consulates are included, but raising hard questions about a tiered system where only those who can pay get a fast interview.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Released the Results of the Exam That Decides a Million College Futures
news.excerpt: The National Testing Agency declared the CUET UG 2026 scorecards on Tuesday for the roughly 1.16 million students who sat the country's single largest gateway to central-university seats — and for the first time, the number of women taking it has drawn almost level with men, a quiet shift that the diaspora's own college-bound families will feel directly.
news.image_caption: A university campus in India; the NTA declared CUET UG 2026 results on June 23 for roughly 1.16 million candidates
news.nri_angle: CUET is increasingly the door diaspora families' own children walk through for an Indian undergraduate education, and NRI/OCI applicants are measured against the same scorecard and the same fast-moving counselling calendar that the NTA's results just set in motion — a deadline that does not bend for families operating across time zones.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

news.title: India Just Rewrote the Rules on Foreign Money for Its Charities — and Diaspora Donors Are in the Frame
news.excerpt: A new Home Ministry notification forces NGOs to name the ultimate source behind donor-advised funds and intermediary vehicles, bars most foreign nationals from running them, and excludes proselytisation — tightening the pipe through which billions in diaspora generosity reaches India each year.
news.image_caption: A government building in New Delhi; the Union Home Ministry tightened FCRA foreign-funding rules for NGOs in a June 2026 gazette notification
news.nri_angle: NRIs and OCIs are among the largest sources of the foreign contributions these rules govern — much of it flowing through the donor-advised funds and intermediary platforms the new disclosure rule targets — so diaspora donors should expect Indian charities to now name them as the ultimate source, and will increasingly need to verify a charity's FCRA compliance before they give.
news.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Diaspora Famous for Sending Money Home Just Pledged $1 Million to Feed Americans Instead
nri-world.excerpt: The HungerMitao movement, built on the slogan 'give where you live,' is quietly redirecting Indian-American philanthropy toward the country the community actually lives in.
nri-world.image_caption: Volunteers pack food donations at the Capital Area Food Bank in the U.S. (Wikimedia Commons)
nri-world.nri_angle: HungerMitao reframes who the diaspora is responsible for — arguing an Indian-American shares a moral claim with a hungry neighbour in their own US city, not only with causes back in India. It is both a unifying force across a fragmented community and a statement of belonging.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: A Cricket Legend and a Blind Industrialist Walked Into a Charity Gala. The Diaspora Opened Its Wallet.
nri-world.excerpt: At the Sankara Eye Foundation's annual fundraiser, Sunil Gavaskar's autographed bats and Srikanth Bolla's life story turned nostalgia into surgeries for the blind back in India.
nri-world.image_caption: Former India captain Sunil Gavaskar, who headlined the Sankara Eye Foundation's diaspora fundraising gala
nri-world.nri_angle: Diaspora philanthropy that funds free eye surgeries in India shows how NRI giving has institutionalised — audited charities, celebrity draws, named sponsor tiers — as a way for immigrants to stay tethered to home and pass that obligation to American-raised children.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Each Summer, a Building-Sized Chariot Rolls Down a North American Street. That's the Whole Point.
nri-world.excerpt: The Ratha Yatra has become the diaspora's most outward-facing ritual — staged on public streets from New York to Vancouver, designed for the neighbours who have never set foot in a temple.
nri-world.image_caption: Devotees pull a towering chariot during an ISKCON Ratha Yatra procession
nri-world.nri_angle: Unlike inward-looking diaspora gatherings, the Ratha Yatra is staged in public for a non-Indian audience — inverting the exclusivity of the Puri original, doing cheap and effective soft-power work, and giving American- and Canadian-raised children a sensory link to a tradition their parents left behind.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Two American Doctors Got One of India's Highest Honours This Week. Both Left India Decades Ago.
nri-world.excerpt: At the second Padma investiture of 2026, President Droupadi Murmu pinned the Padma Bhushan on a New York radiation oncologist and the Padma Shri on a Kansas gastroenterologist — a reminder that India still counts the diaspora's achievements as its own.
nri-world.image_caption: Dr Dattatreyudu Nori receiving a Padma award at a Civil Investiture Ceremony at Rashtrapati Bhavan; the New York radiation oncologist was conferred the Padma Bhushan in 2026
nri-world.nri_angle: Indian-origin doctors are one of the diaspora's biggest contributions to the West — a huge share of physicians in the US and UK — yet they rarely get formal recognition from the homeland; pinning a Padma Bhushan and a Padma Shri on two American-based physicians is India publicly counting the medical diaspora's success as its own, and telling emigrant families that a foreign passport and decades abroad don't cut the tie.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Britain's Big India Summit Left London This Year. It Went to the Midlands Instead.
nri-world.excerpt: The 10th UK-India Week opened at the University of Warwick, with a Gujarat delegation courting West Midlands leaders on investment, skills and clean energy — a sign that the diaspora's economic diplomacy is moving out of the capital and into Britain's industrial heartland.
nri-world.image_caption: The University of Warwick in the West Midlands, which hosted the opening of the 10th UK-India Week in 2026
nri-world.nri_angle: Britain's largest concentration of Indian-origin families and businesses sits outside London, in places like the West Midlands; moving UK-India Week's regions forum to the University of Warwick — and pairing a Gujarat delegation with Midlands leaders — is an attempt to turn the diaspora's informal, decades-old family and professional networks into formal investment pipelines, university tie-ups and clean-energy and manufacturing deals.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Diaspora Has Spent 20 Years Collecting Trophies. India Just Handed It a Database Instead.
nri-world.excerpt: At a New Jersey gala for Indian-American achievers, the Consul General launched a free trade portal — and asked the room for its address book, not its cash.
nri-world.image_caption: The global spread of the Indian diaspora, now the world's largest
nri-world.nri_angle: The India-USA Trade Facilitation Portal reframes the diaspora's economic role: not remittances, but using its knowledge of American markets to connect small Indian exporters with US buyers as part of the $500bn Mission 500 trade target.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Says NRIs Can Buy Its Mutual Funds. For Indians in America and Canada, Most Fund Houses Say No Anyway.
nri-world.excerpt: The barrier isn't Indian law — it's FATCA. Only eight to ten of India's 44 fund houses will onboard US and Canadian NRIs, pushing the diaspora's richest cohort toward GIFT City workarounds.
nri-world.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street, Mumbai
nri-world.nri_angle: The US and Canadian diaspora — India's wealthiest and most courted overseas communities — are the ones most often locked out of Indian mutual funds, because FATCA compliance costs make AMCs refuse them. A structural exclusion built into the diaspora's tax status.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Washington Has a Museum for Almost Everyone. A Group of Indian-Americans Is Tired of the Gap.
nri-world.excerpt: After eight years validating 11,000 years of history, the team behind the India Heritage Center wants a $14 million permanent home for India's story in the US capital.
nri-world.image_caption: The National Mall in Washington; Indian-Americans are pushing for a museum to mark their place in the American story
nri-world.nri_angle: A second-generation anxiety made physical: as Indian-Americans reach the center of US life, they worry their children are losing the connection to India's history. The India Heritage Center is a bet that a permanent museum in Washington can hold that thread.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Has 31 Million People Abroad. Until This Week, It Didn't Have a Working Phone Book.
nri-world.excerpt: Delhi's new Global Pravasi Rishta portal isn't a grievance desk — it's the diaspora register the government wished it had during every recent overseas crisis.
nri-world.nri_angle: A single MEA portal that lets every NRI, OCI and PIO register once with their local Indian mission — for event invites, scheme info, and faster contact in a crisis or evacuation.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: Indian-Americans Are 1.5% of the Country. They Pay 5-6% of Its Income Taxes.
nri-world.excerpt: A first-of-its-kind Indiaspora report puts hard numbers on diaspora success — and arrives just as the community's place in US politics turns contentious.
nri-world.image_caption: A culturally diverse team in a business meeting
nri-world.nri_angle: A data-driven case for belonging: the report reframes Indian-American immigration debates in the language of net fiscal and economic contribution, just as H-1B scrutiny intensifies.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: The Diaspora Used to Ask Britain to Let It In. This Week It Hosted the Conversation in the House of Lords.
nri-world.excerpt: A 'Viksit Bharat 2047' forum in Parliament's upper chamber showed how far Britain's Indians have travelled — and how much now rides on a trade deal that keeps slipping.
nri-world.image_caption: The House of Lords chamber in the Palace of Westminster, London
nri-world.nri_angle: Britain's Indian community is now its most economically successful minority; an event in the House of Lords about India's 2047 vision marks the moment that success starts converting into political voice — with the stalled India-UK FTA the real test of whether the 'living bridge' becomes infrastructure.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

nri-world.title: India Wants the Diaspora's Dollars Back. It's Offering 7.1% — and a $55 Billion Bet — to Get Them.
nri-world.excerpt: A revived RBI swap scheme has touched off an FCNR deposit rate war. For NRIs the returns are real, but the fine print on lock-ins and tax is where the deal is won or lost.
nri-world.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India headquarters in Mumbai
nri-world.nri_angle: The RBI's FCNR(B) swap subsidy is, in effect, a fundraising drive aimed squarely at the 35-million-strong diaspora's savings — offering tax-advantaged dollar returns up to 7.1%, but with three-to-five-year lock-ins and FATCA/FBAR/TDS complications that NRIs must weigh before chasing the headline rate.
nri-world.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India’s Economy Just Cooled to a Three-Month Low — and a Resurgent Dollar Is Squeezing the Rupee Again
markets-finance.excerpt: Fresh data show India’s private-sector growth slowing and business confidence at its weakest in nearly four years, just as rising bets on a U.S. Federal Reserve rate hike push the dollar to a one-year high and drag the rupee and Indian stocks lower.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai; Indian markets pulled back as growth cooled and a stronger dollar pressured the rupee
markets-finance.nri_angle: For NRIs, the twin pressures matter directly: a weaker rupee stretches the value of dollars sent home or invested in India, while a cooling economy and a hawkish Fed reshape the calculus on when to remit, when to buy Indian equities, and how much currency risk to carry.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is Courting the Diaspora’s Dollars to Rescue the Rupee — and Banks Are Racing to Cash In
markets-finance.excerpt: The RBI is subsidising hedging costs on foreign-currency deposits and now letting domestic banks lend against them, in a 2013-style push to pull tens of billions of NRI dollars into the country. Analysts estimate the scheme could draw anywhere from $55 billion to $100 billion.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India is courting diaspora dollars through high-yield foreign-currency deposits to defend the rupee
markets-finance.nri_angle: This scheme is aimed squarely at NRIs: with banks now offering 6–7 percent on dollar deposits — and leveraged structures that could push returns toward 12–15 percent — overseas Indians can earn high rupee-equivalent yields without taking on currency risk, while helping defend the very rupee their families back home depend on.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Reliance Lays Out a Five-Year Plan to Double Its Earnings — With AI and the Sun at the Centre
markets-finance.excerpt: At its 49th AGM, Mukesh Ambani's conglomerate paired a record-profit year with bold targets: doubling consolidated EBITDA, a ₹1-trillion FMCG business, an AI push across every product, and 200,000 green-energy jobs — even as the stock trades well below its peak.
markets-finance.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani used Reliance's 49th AGM to set a five-year target of doubling the conglomerate's core earnings
markets-finance.nri_angle: Reliance is the single heaviest weight in the Sensex and Nifty that anchor most NRI India portfolios and mutual-fund SIPs, so its five-year bet on AI, consumer brands and solar energy is, in effect, a bet on the direction of the entire market the diaspora invests in — and a preview of where India's economy is trying to go.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Just Bought More Russian Oil Than Ever — Right as Washington's Sanctions Waiver Expires
markets-finance.excerpt: After the Iran war scrambled global energy flows, Russia's share of India's crude imports has nearly doubled to almost half, hitting a record 2.55 million barrels a day in June — but a lapsed US waiver now forces a tricky choice on Delhi's refiners.
markets-finance.image_caption: Russia now supplies almost half of India's crude imports, with a record 2.55 million barrels a day arriving in June
markets-finance.nri_angle: India's energy bill is the hidden hinge of its economy — it shapes inflation, the rupee NRIs send money in, and the stock indices the diaspora invests in — so how Delhi balances cheap Russian crude against renewed US sanctions pressure will ripple straight through the remittances and portfolios that tie the diaspora to home.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: An Accenture Warning Knocks Indian IT — and the Bigger Fear Is What It Signals for Next Year
markets-finance.excerpt: After the world's largest IT services firm trimmed its revenue outlook, Indian software giants like Infosys, TCS and Wipro slid as much as 7 percent, and brokerages warned that the coming financial year could prove tougher than the market has been pricing in.
markets-finance.image_caption: Indian IT majors slid sharply after Accenture trimmed its revenue guidance, dragging the Nifty IT index lower
markets-finance.nri_angle: Indian IT is the diaspora's bellwether industry — it employs many NRIs' relatives, anchors the portfolios of those who invest back home, and underpins the H-1B pipeline that brought a generation to America — so a warning that demand and AI are squeezing the sector touches NRI jobs, savings and family fortunes at once.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Faces Its Weakest Monsoon in 11 Years — but This Time the Economy Is Better Armoured
markets-finance.excerpt: A strengthening El Niño has delayed the rains and brought dangerous heat, threatening harvests, food prices and growth. Yet bigger reservoirs and far wider irrigation mean the damage may be more contained than the alarming headlines suggest.
markets-finance.image_caption: India faces its weakest monsoon in 11 years as a strengthening El Niño delays the rains and brings dangerous heat
markets-finance.nri_angle: A poor monsoon feeds straight into the things NRIs watch most closely about India — food inflation that erodes the rupee's value, the central bank's room to cut rates, and the strength of the currency their remittances and investments are denominated in — making this year's rains a quiet but real input into diaspora financial decisions.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Gold Was Supposed to Soar During the Iran War. It Fell Nearly 10% Instead — Now JP Morgan Sees a 40% Rebound
markets-finance.excerpt: The metal that diaspora families trust as a crisis hedge defied its safe-haven reputation, sliding even as conflict raged, before steadying near ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams. The episode is a sharp lesson in how gold really behaves — and why timing it is a fool's errand.
markets-finance.image_caption: Gold fell nearly 10% in India during the Iran war despite its safe-haven reputation, before steadying near ₹1.46 lakh per 10 grams
markets-finance.nri_angle: Gold is the diaspora's instinctive store of value — bought for weddings, gifted at festivals, hoarded as insurance against bad times — so its counter-intuitive slide during an actual war, and the debate over where it goes next, speaks directly to how NRIs should size and time their single most emotional investment.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The RBI Burned Through Nearly $9 Billion in a Single Month Defending the Rupee — and Reserves Are at a One-Year Low
markets-finance.excerpt: Fresh central bank data show the Reserve Bank of India sold a net $8.9 billion in April to slow the rupee's slide, capping a record fiscal year of intervention as foreign reserves fell to $671.6 billion and the currency clawed back from an all-time low.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India sold a net $8.9 billion in April to defend the rupee, with forex reserves falling to a one-year low
markets-finance.nri_angle: The scale of the RBI's dollar-selling tells NRIs how hard their central bank is working to keep the rupee from sliding further — a direct signal on the value of remittances, NRE and FCNR deposits, and India-bound investments, and on whether the recent record lows are a floor or a way station.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: The Rupee Just Had Its Best Week in Months. Now a Resurgent Dollar Will Test Whether It Holds.
markets-finance.excerpt: A drop in oil after the US-Iran peace deal pushed the rupee to 94.32, its strongest weekly run in 11 weeks — but a dollar at a one-year high and a hawkish Federal Reserve are pulling the currency back, while government bonds wait on the pace of foreign money returning.
markets-finance.image_caption: The rupee posted its best week in months as oil prices fell, before a resurgent dollar tested the gains
markets-finance.nri_angle: Every move in the rupee reprices the remittances NRIs send home, the value of their NRE and FCNR deposits, and the returns on their Indian investments — so a week that swung from oil-driven relief to dollar-driven pressure is not abstract macro news for the diaspora but a direct signal on when to send money and what their India holdings are worth.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Ambani's Jio Files for What Could Be India's Biggest IPO Ever — and This Time, No One Is Cashing Out
markets-finance.excerpt: Jio Platforms has filed draft papers with India's markets regulator for a fresh-issue-only listing of up to 27 crore shares, a deal market estimates put near ₹36,000 crore at a valuation of roughly ₹12.5 lakh crore — with the proceeds aimed squarely at paying down debt rather than handing existing investors an exit.
markets-finance.image_caption: Reliance Industries chairman Mukesh Ambani, whose Jio Platforms has filed draft papers for a record IPO
markets-finance.nri_angle: Jio touches nearly every Indian family with a phone, and its listing is the marquee event NRI investors have waited years for — a chance to own a slice of the diaspora's most-used digital utility, even as the fresh-issue-only structure and a cooled, war-rattled market raise real questions about price and timing.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: Foreigners Keep Selling Indian Stocks. Indians Keep Buying — and That Has Quietly Rewired the Market
markets-finance.excerpt: In May, foreign investors pulled nearly Rs 33,000 crore out of Indian equities while domestic institutions poured in over Rs 82,000 crore — powered by a record Rs 30,954 crore of monthly SIP contributions across 9.64 crore accounts — a structural shift that means the old reflex of watching foreign flows to call the market is increasingly out of date.
markets-finance.image_caption: Domestic mutual fund inflows have grown large enough to absorb foreign investors' selling of Indian equities
markets-finance.nri_angle: Many NRIs still read foreign-investor outflows as a sell signal for Indian stocks, but a steady tide of domestic SIP money is now large enough to absorb that selling — a shift that should reframe how the diaspora thinks about timing, volatility and where the Indian market's real support now comes from.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

markets-finance.title: India Is Dangling Higher Dollar Rates to Pull NRI Money Home — and Banks Now Want to Route It Through GIFT City
markets-finance.excerpt: After the RBI agreed to absorb the hedging cost on fresh foreign-currency NRI deposits and scrapped the rate caps, banks have pushed dollar deposit rates to 6–7 percent and are seeking permission to fund the inflows through their offshore GIFT City units — part of a drive analysts think could draw $55 billion or more to steady the rupee.
markets-finance.image_caption: The Reserve Bank of India has sweetened terms on foreign-currency NRI deposits to draw the diaspora's dollars and steady the rupee
markets-finance.nri_angle: This drive is aimed squarely at the diaspora's wallet: NRIs can suddenly earn 6–7 percent on dollar deposits in Indian banks — nearly double the old rates and with no currency risk — making it one of the most consequential personal-finance shifts for overseas Indians in years.
markets-finance.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India's Women Sprinters Beat China for Relay Gold — a Statement Beyond the Javelin
sports.excerpt: At the Asian Relays Championships in Shangyu, India's women's 4x100m quartet ran down the host nation for gold, and a mixed-relay silver and bronze signalled that the country's track ambitions are spreading well past Neeraj Chopra.
sports.image_caption: Srabani Nanda, part of India's gold-winning women's 4x100m relay quartet at the 2026 Asian Relays Championships in Shangyu, China.
sports.nri_angle: Indian athletics has rested almost entirely on Neeraj Chopra's javelin; a women's sprint relay gold won by beating host China broadens that story with new names, just weeks before the Glasgow Commonwealth Games and with India set to host the next Asian Relays in Chandigarh in 2027 — a fresh rallying point for NRIs invested in India's Olympic ambitions.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Rishabh Pant Is Going Home to Delhi — and He Took a 12-Crore Pay Cut to Get There
sports.excerpt: The IPL has confirmed the season's biggest trade: Pant returns to Delhi Capitals for INR 15 crore while Kuldeep Yadav heads to Lucknow, unwinding the record deal that made Pant the most expensive cricketer in the league's history.
sports.image_caption: Rishabh Pant, who returns to Delhi Capitals in the IPL 2027 trade window after two seasons with Lucknow Super Giants
sports.nri_angle: The IPL is the diaspora's loudest shared spring ritual, and Pant's pay-cut homecoming to Delhi — days after NRIs celebrated his Headingley century — is exactly the kind of franchise drama Indians abroad follow as closely as any match.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Fifteen Golds in Mersin: India's Young Para-Shuttlers Just Announced the Next Generation
sports.excerpt: India finished the 2026 World Abilitysport Youth Games in Türkiye with 27 para-badminton medals — 15 of them gold — spread across every classification, a haul that points to a pipeline far deeper than its Paralympic stars alone.
sports.image_caption: Indian para-badminton international Mansi Joshi in 2020 (file photo); India's youth squad won 27 para-badminton medals in Mersin
sports.nri_angle: India's para-badminton has become a global powerhouse, and this youth haul signals the next generation — a point of pride for NRI families raising children in inclusion-focused Western systems and a sign that the pathway in para-sport now exists in India too.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Lose Another All-Rounder Before England — and Hand a Mumbai Newcomer His First Cap
sports.excerpt: Nitish Kumar Reddy has been ruled out of India's T20I tours of Ireland and England with a quadriceps injury, and the selectors have responded by drafting in the uncapped Mumbai all-rounder Suryansh Shedge for his maiden call-up.
sports.image_caption: India all-rounder Nitish Kumar Reddy, ruled out of the Ireland and England T20Is with a quadriceps injury
sports.nri_angle: India's Ireland and England white-ball summer is the most accessible tour for UK and Irish NRIs in years, and the all-rounder reshuffle — Reddy out, Pandya out, an uncapped Mumbai name in — will directly shape the XI diaspora crowds see at Belfast and English grounds.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Eleven Balls: A 15-Year-Old Just Broke the Fastest-Fifty Record in 50-Over Cricket
sports.excerpt: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi reached his half-century in 11 deliveries for India A against Sri Lanka A in Dambulla, the quickest in the history of List A cricket — a record-breaking innings of 94 off 29 days before the teenager is set to become India's youngest ever men's international.
sports.image_caption: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi, the 15-year-old who hit the fastest fifty in List A history
sports.nri_angle: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi is the prodigy the entire cricket-following diaspora is tracking — his record 11-ball fifty comes just as he is named for India's tours of Ireland and England, putting a likely record-breaking debut within reach of NRI crowds and making him the must-watch name of the summer.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Five Hundreds Were Not Enough: England Chase 371 at Headingley, and India's New Era Opens With a Defeat
sports.excerpt: Ben Duckett's brilliant 149 carried England to 373 for 5 and a five-wicket win on the final day, leaving India the first team in Test history to lose a match in which it scored five individual centuries — a chastening start to Shubman Gill's captaincy.
sports.image_caption: Ben Duckett, whose 149 powered England's chase of 371 at Headingley
sports.nri_angle: A new India era under captain Shubman Gill — the first Test of the post-Kohli, post-Rohit transition — opened with a wrenching defeat despite five individual centuries. For the large British-Indian crowd at Headingley and NRIs watching across the US, Canada and the Gulf, it was a sobering, unforgettable start to a new chapter of the team they follow most closely.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: MI New York Found Their Feet in Texas, and an Edison-Raised Captain Led the Way Home
sports.excerpt: A night after their season opened with a stumble, the Mumbai Indians' American franchise dismantled the Texas Super Kings for 158 and chased it down with eight wickets to spare — USA captain Monank Patel anchoring, Nicholas Pooran finishing unbeaten on 68.
sports.image_caption: Trent Boult, who took 3 for 18 to help bowl out the Texas Super Kings for 158
sports.nri_angle: Major League Cricket is the competition the Indian-American community helped build, and MI New York's first win of 2026 was anchored by Monank Patel — the New Jersey-raised USA captain — a hometown hero for NRIs following top-tier T20 cricket on American soil.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: Three Centuries, One Collapse: India Pile Up 471 at Headingley, Then Watch England Punch Straight Back
sports.excerpt: Yashasvi Jaiswal, Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant all reached three figures on a sun-soaked Leeds morning — yet India lost their last seven wickets for 41, and by stumps Ollie Pope's unbeaten hundred had England right back in the contest.
sports.image_caption: Rishabh Pant, whose stylish 134 was the highlight of India's first innings at Headingley
sports.nri_angle: The first Test of India's post-Kohli, post-Rohit era is captivating the diaspora: three hometown heroes — Jaiswal, captain Gill and the inspirational comeback man Rishabh Pant — all scored hundreds at Headingley, yet a classic lower-order collapse kept England in the game, a drama NRIs across the US, UK and Canada are following ball by ball.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: No Indian in the Singles Again: At Wimbledon, the Flag Now Travels in the Doubles Draw
sports.excerpt: As Wimbledon qualifying began this week, India had no man or woman in any Grand Slam singles main draw for a second straight year. The tricolour at SW19 will be carried by its doubles specialists — and, in a twist, by an Indian-American who could never play for India.
sports.image_caption: Yuki Bhambri, India's top-ranked doubles player, leads a doubles-only Indian contingent at Wimbledon 2026
sports.nri_angle: For a second straight year no Indian features in Grand Slam singles, so the tricolour at Wimbledon travels in the doubles draw — carried by an Indian Army subedar in the form of his life and a veteran reborn in the two-man game — while the diaspora's biggest SW19 story is Rajeev Ram, the Indian-American former World No. 1 who once tried, and failed, to play for India.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: One Defeat Turned India's World Cup Into a Tightrope: Beat Australia, or Trust a Calculator
sports.excerpt: A shock loss to South Africa has stripped away India's safety net at the Women's T20 World Cup. Harmanpreet Kaur's side must now get past Bangladesh and the six-time champions to be sure of the semi-finals.
sports.image_caption: India captain Harmanpreet Kaur, whose side must navigate a virtual knockout to reach the semi-finals
sports.nri_angle: The Indian women's team has become appointment viewing across the diaspora, and its June 28 virtual knockout against Australia at Lord's — a ground steeped in NRI pilgrimage — is the sort of fixture that fills WhatsApp groups from London to New Jersey, with a generation of diaspora girls now growing up on Harmanpreet and Mandhana.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Sacked the Captain Who Won Them the T20 World Cup — and Left Him Out of the Team Altogether
sports.excerpt: Months after Suryakumar Yadav lifted India's third T20 world title, the selectors have stripped him of the captaincy and his place in the side. Shreyas Iyer, back in the format after two and a half years, inherits the job.
sports.image_caption: Shreyas Iyer, recalled after more than two years, is India's new full-time T20I captain
sports.nri_angle: A World Cup-winning captain dropped months after the trophy lift is a Rorschach test for the diaspora — cold-blooded modernity to some, betrayal to others — and a window on how ruthless India have become about staying atop the white-ball game, the kind of loyalty-versus-results debate that runs hot in NRI WhatsApp groups across time zones.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

sports.title: India Picked Its England One-Day Squad, and the Team Sheet Read Like a Changing of the Guard
sports.excerpt: Shubman Gill now captains India in all three formats, Jasprit Bumrah is back, and Yashasvi Jaiswal was left out despite a match-winning hundred. Virat Kohli is in too — if his hamstring lets him be.
sports.image_caption: Shubman Gill, who now captains India across all three formats, will lead the ODI side in England
sports.nri_angle: A squad sheet that captures a generational handover the diaspora has followed with tenderness — the team passing from Kohli and Rohit to Shubman Gill, who now captains across all formats — while the dropping of a centurion (Jaiswal) is exactly the kind of selection debate that lights up NRI WhatsApp groups across time zones, all framed against India's build toward the 2027 ODI World Cup.
sports.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India's Quietest AI Investor Just Showed Its Hand: Rs 1,003 Crore Across 54 Startups
technology.excerpt: Info Edge, the firm behind Naukri and an early Zomato backer, carved out its AI and deeptech bets as a separate book for the first time — and was unusually frank about how few have paid off yet.
technology.image_caption: Founders at work in a startup office, the kind of early-stage company Info Edge's deeptech funds back
technology.nri_angle: For NRIs who treat Info Edge as a proxy for India's internet economy, the disclosure is a rare honest map of where smart Indian capital is betting on AI — and a reminder that the deeptech wave is still years from returns.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: A Bengaluru Startup Wants to Build India's Largest Security Operations Centre. Bessemer Just Bet $15 Million on It.
technology.excerpt: Mitigata raised a Series B less than a year after its last round, betting that AI-driven attacks and a chronic talent shortage have created a 'perfect storm' for Indian enterprises.
technology.image_caption: A security operations workstation, the kind of monitoring infrastructure cyber-resilience firms run around the clock
technology.nri_angle: NRIs increasingly hold accounts, run businesses and store data with Indian banks and firms — the institutions Mitigata is racing to protect — making India's cyber-resilience build-out a direct concern for the diaspora, not a distant domestic story.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Has a New Real-Estate Unicorn. The Twist Is How It Got There — and Who's Buying.
technology.excerpt: Square Yards crossed a $1 billion valuation on a Rs 900 crore debt-and-equity round, riding a property platform built in no small part on the wallets of non-resident Indians.
technology.image_caption: Modern residential apartment towers of the kind sold on India's online property platforms
technology.nri_angle: Square Yards built its business partly by selling Indian property to NRIs — so its rise to unicorn status is, in a literal sense, a story about where the diaspora's money has been going.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Razorpay Came Home to India, Then Quietly Filed to Go Public. The Reverse-Flip Era Has Its Marquee Test.
technology.excerpt: The payments giant filed confidential IPO papers with SEBI, seeking up to $700 million at a valuation reset to $5-6 billion. After a costly move from Delaware back to Bengaluru, its listing is a referendum on whether Indian startups belong on Indian exchanges.
technology.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange building on Dalal Street, Mumbai. Razorpay has filed confidential IPO papers with SEBI, aiming for a main-board listing on India's exchanges.
technology.nri_angle: For NRIs who built or backed Indian startups through US holding structures, Razorpay's expensive journey home and its listing on an Indian exchange is the clearest signal yet that the centre of gravity for Indian tech value creation has shifted from Delaware and Nasdaq back to Bengaluru and Dalal Street.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: An AI That Refuses to Answer Until It Can Prove It Is Right. IIT Madras Alumni Just Raised $27 Million to Build It.
technology.excerpt: Pramaana Labs, backed by Vinod Khosla, is wrapping large language models in mathematical proof engines so AI can be trusted in tax, law and medicine. Half its team sits in India — a bet that the next AI breakthrough is reliability, not raw intelligence.
technology.image_caption: Vinod Khosla, whose firm Khosla Ventures led Pramaana Labs' $27 million seed round. The Indian-American venture capitalist was an early backer of OpenAI.
technology.nri_angle: Founded by IIT Madras alumni with half its workforce in India and led by a round from Indian-American legend Vinod Khosla, Pramaana embodies the US-India deep-tech bridge: the hardest problems in AI being attacked by Indian engineering talent on both sides of the Pacific.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: A Swiggy Rider Can Now Start a Mutual Fund in a Few Taps. India Just Wired Investing Into the Gig Economy.
technology.excerpt: Swiggy's tie-up with Zerodha Fund House lets delivery partners invest from Rs 100 straight through their rider app. It is a small feature with a big idea behind it — formal finance reaching the people the formal economy usually skips.
technology.image_caption: A Swiggy delivery partner on the road in India. Riders can now invest part of their earnings in mutual funds through the same app they use for deliveries.
technology.nri_angle: For NRIs who hold Swiggy stock or watch India's fintech rails, this is a live test of whether digital public infrastructure can pull millions of informal workers into formal investing — the next frontier after UPI moved money and Aadhaar moved identity.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Foreign Satellite Giants Are Stuck at India's Door. Mukesh Ambani Just Decided to Build His Own Constellation.
technology.excerpt: As Starlink and Amazon wait on Delhi's security clearances, Jio says it will build a sovereign low-Earth-orbit network for India — a bet that connectivity from space should be Indian-owned.
technology.image_caption: An artist's impression of a low-Earth-orbit satellite constellation. Jio says it will build a sovereign LEO network for India.
technology.nri_angle: NRIs who send devices, money and expectations of connectivity back to rural India have a direct stake in who controls the satellite broadband that finally reaches the village — a foreign operator on a licence, or a sovereign Indian network built to stay.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Indians Are Putting Solar on the Roof Faster Than Anyone Expected. Investors Just Poured Rs 510 Crore Into the Company Riding That Wave.
technology.excerpt: SolarSquare's new funding round, led by Lightspeed, is a bet that rooftop solar has crossed from subsidy story to consumer habit — powered by the PM Surya Ghar scheme and rising electricity bills.
technology.image_caption: Rooftop solar panels on homes in Mehsana, Gujarat. India's residential solar market is drawing major venture capital.
technology.nri_angle: For NRIs funding solar panels on the family home back in India, or eyeing the country's clean-energy boom as an investment, SolarSquare's raise marks the moment rooftop solar stopped being a green gesture and became a mainstream consumer purchase.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: India Just Approved Its First Silicon-Carbide Fab. The Map of Where Chips Get Made Is Quietly Shifting East.
technology.excerpt: Four new projects in Odisha, Punjab and Andhra take India's chip mission to 10 plants and Rs 1.6 lakh crore. For diaspora engineers, the question is whether the jobs follow the press releases.
technology.image_caption: A 200mm semiconductor wafer fabrication line, the kind of facility India is now building across multiple states
technology.nri_angle: For Indian-American chip engineers weighing a move home, the spread of fabs beyond Gujarat into Odisha, Punjab and Andhra is the first sign the semiconductor mission might create real careers, not just ribbon-cuttings.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Sundar Pichai Spent Three Years Being Called Late to AI. Google's Cloud Backlog Just Hit $460 Billion.
technology.excerpt: A near-doubling of signed cloud commitments in a single quarter is the clearest sign yet that Pichai's full-stack AI bet is paying off — and it reshapes the job math for Indians inside Google.
technology.image_caption: Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai
technology.nri_angle: For the thousands of Indian engineers at Google weighing AI-era job security, a $460 billion cloud backlog signals where the company is hiring and investing — and which teams are safest as the AI reorganisation grinds on.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: Ola Electric Built India's Biggest Scooter Factory. Its Quieter Rival Is Opening a Store a Day.
technology.excerpt: As Ather expands toward 1,100 outlets and Ola shrinks from 4,000 to 700, India's electric-two-wheeler race has flipped from a land grab to a test of who can actually make money.
technology.image_caption: Ola Electric scooters, India's best-known electric two-wheeler brand
technology.nri_angle: NRI investors who bought into the India EV story through Ola's or Ather's listings now face a clearer divide: the flashy market-share leader is retreating while the disciplined rival expands, and the gap explains which bet is holding up.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

technology.title: A Trillion Dollars Vanished From the Nasdaq in a Day. The Engineers Who Built the AI Boom Have the Most to Lose.
technology.excerpt: Tuesday's tech wreck wiped more than $1 trillion off the Nasdaq 100 as investors finally asked whether the debt-funded AI buildout can pay for itself. For Indian techies whose net worth, RSUs and job security ride on these stocks, the reckoning is personal.
technology.image_caption: The Nasdaq MarketSite in Times Square, New York
technology.nri_angle: Tens of thousands of Indian engineers at Nvidia, Google, Microsoft and Micron hold much of their compensation in the very AI stocks now in freefall — a correction that hits their RSUs, mortgages and visa-tethered job security harder than almost anyone.
technology.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: The Dragons Came Back Hungry. 'House of the Dragon' Season 3 Lands on JioHotstar — and It Opens With a Death.
entertainment.excerpt: Eight episodes, weekly drops, and a 72-minute premiere that drowns one of Rhaenyra's sons in the Battle of the Gullet. Here's where the diaspora can watch the bloodiest Targaryen chapter yet.
entertainment.image_caption: Matt Smith returns as Daemon Targaryen in House of the Dragon Season 3 (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Zendaya Is Wearing Spider-Man's Colours Now — and the 'Brand New Day' Press Tour Has Become the Best Show in Town
entertainment.excerpt: Versace chainmail in Rome, leather in Berlin, a 5-carat ring she's no longer hiding, and Tom Holland kissing her forehead between photocalls. The fashion is the marketing now.
entertainment.image_caption: Zendaya on the Spider-Man: Brand New Day press tour (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Rajkumar Hirani Finally Goes Streaming — and Hands His Own Son the Lead. 'Pritam And Pedro' Lands July 3.
entertainment.excerpt: Bollywood's most beloved storyteller makes his OTT debut on JioHotstar with a Goa-set cybercrime comedy. Vir Hirani plays the hacker. Arshad Warsi plays the cop. And the Munna Bhai magic is quietly back in the room.
entertainment.image_caption: Filmmaker Rajkumar Hirani, whose OTT debut Pritam And Pedro premieres on JioHotstar on July 3 (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: India Just Walked Into the Cannes of Animation. 'Baahubali: The Eternal War' Is Maahishmati's Most Daring Bet Yet.
entertainment.excerpt: SS Rajamouli's animated saga has been picked for the Work in Progress lineup at Annecy 2026 — the world's most prestigious animation stage. Prabhas is back as Baahubali's soul, this time fighting a cosmic war across 14 realms.
entertainment.image_caption: Director SS Rajamouli, whose animated saga Baahubali: The Eternal War was selected for Annecy 2026 (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Allu Arjun Flies to a Mirror, Not a Set. The AA23 Look Test Is the First Real Move in Bollywood-Tollywood's Most Dangerous Team-Up.
entertainment.excerpt: Lokesh Kanagaraj lands in Mumbai on June 25 to lock the face of his Telugu debut. Pushpa's swagger, the LCU's darkness, and Anirudh on the console — the diaspora hasn't been this hungry for a first look in years.
entertainment.image_caption: Allu Arjun, who teams with director Lokesh Kanagaraj for AA23 (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Pandora Comes Home. 'Avatar: Fire and Ash' Lands on JioHotstar This Wednesday — in Hindi, Tamil and Telugu.
entertainment.excerpt: James Cameron's $1.49 billion volcano epic skips the rental wall and drops straight into your living room on June 24. For the diaspora family that never made it to an IMAX screen, the wait is finally over.
entertainment.image_caption: Avatar: Fire and Ash, now streaming on JioHotstar (Wikipedia)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Ranbir Said No. Imran Said No. Saif Ali Khan Said 'Okay, Chal' — and Walked Into a Classic.
entertainment.excerpt: As Cocktail 2 fills theatres, Saif reveals the dirty little secret of the 2012 original: nobody wanted to share the screen with Deepika's Veronica. Their loss became his legend.
entertainment.image_caption: Saif Ali Khan, who played Gautam in the 2012 hit Cocktail (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

entertainment.title: Arjun Rampal Is Playing a Fallen Billionaire. The Producer Just Admitted Who He's 'Loosely Based' On.
entertainment.excerpt: Hansal Mehta's next is 'Billionaire', and the industry's worst-kept secret is finally semi-official: that swagger, that empire, that spectacular fall belong to a tycoon we all know the name of.
entertainment.image_caption: Arjun Rampal, who leads the upcoming Amazon MX Player series Billionaire (Wikimedia Commons)
entertainment.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A High-Dose Omega-3 Pill Reached the Brain but Did Nothing for Memory, a Gold-Standard Trial Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a two-year randomized trial of older adults at risk of dementia, daily fish-oil-style DHA more than doubled omega-3 levels in the blood and reached the brain — yet it failed to improve memory, thinking or the size of the brain’s memory centre any more than a placebo.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Omega-3 fish-oil capsules; a two-year randomized trial found high-dose DHA reached the brain but did not improve memory
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Fish-oil and omega-3 capsules are among the most popular over-the-counter supplements in Indian-origin households, often bought in bulk and taken for years in the belief they protect the aging brain; this rigorous trial is a reminder that for most people the money may be better spent on diet and exercise than on a daily pill.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: It May Not Be How Much Protein You Eat, but Which Building Blocks — a New Longevity-Diet Study Suggests
lifestyle-health.excerpt: Scientists at USC report that fine-tuning a single amino acid, methionine, let mice eat more food yet lose fat without losing muscle — and that people eating the most animal protein had twice the rate of diabetes, hinting the kind of protein may matter more than the amount.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Lentils and legumes; new research suggests the type of protein, not just the amount, may shape metabolic health
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: The protein debate cuts to the heart of diaspora eating habits — from the dal-and-rice plant-based traditions of many Indian households to the high-protein, meat-heavy regimes popular in Western fitness culture — and this research suggests the traditional emphasis on plant proteins may carry an underappreciated metabolic advantage.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Joint-Pain Supplement Millions Take May Quietly Speed Up Alzheimer’s, a New Study Warns
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study in Nature Metabolism finds that glucosamine — one of the world’s most popular supplements for aching knees — fuels a sugar build-up in the brain that worsened memory in mice and was tied to faster decline and higher death rates in people with dementia.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Dietary supplement capsules; a new study links glucosamine to a sugar build-up that worsened Alzheimer’s in mice and people
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Glucosamine is a staple in the supplement cabinets of older Indian-origin adults managing arthritis and knee pain, often taken for years without a doctor’s oversight; this study is an early but sobering signal that anyone in a diaspora family already living with memory loss should review the habit with a physician rather than assume a 'natural' joint pill is harmless.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Four Minutes a Day Was Enough to Make Frail Older Adults Steadier on Their Feet, a Trial Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A home-based program of just four simple exercises — done daily for half a minute each — measurably improved leg strength, balance and the ability to rise from a chair in inactive adults over 65, with most participants sticking to it 81 percent of the time.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: An older adult exercising at home; a four-minute daily routine improved balance and leg strength in adults over 65
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Aging Indian-origin parents — many living with their children abroad, often sedentary through long winters and culturally hesitant about gyms — are precisely the group this study targets: a four-minute, no-equipment-heavy routine doable in a living room is a realistic way for diaspora families to help elders stay independent and avoid the falls that so often trigger a cascade of decline.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Why Poor Sleep Harms Some Brains More Than Others May Come Down to a Single Gene
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new study of a brain-cleaning gene called AQP4 found that the same sleep habits can speed or slow early Alzheimer's-type changes depending on which version of the gene a person carries — a clue to why two people who sleep alike can age so differently.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A normal brain compared with an Alzheimer's-affected brain; a gene called AQP4 may shape how sleep affects early decline (Wikimedia Commons)
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Sleep is one of the few dementia risk factors anyone can actually change, and for a diaspora that often runs on jet lag, late shifts and a strong family history of dementia, the finding that a person's genes decide how much their sleep matters is a practical nudge to treat rest as preventive medicine, not a luxury.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Dangerous Heat Now Reaches More of the World — and the Nights Are No Longer a Refuge
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new analysis finds the share of the planet exposed to severe heat stress climbed from 16% to 22% over fifty years, with brutal heat spreading into regions that never knew it and ‘tropical nights’ stripping away the body's chance to cool down and recover.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A new study finds severe heat stress now reaches 22% of the world's population, up from 16% five decades ago
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Heat is a health story that bridges the diaspora's two worlds at once — family in Indian cities enduring some of the planet's most punishing summers, and relatives in the UK, North America and Scandinavia now facing heat their homes were never built for, making this a rare risk that touches both ends of the migration journey.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Weight-Loss Drug That Was Feared to Weaken Bones May Actually Help Protect Them
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In a study of nearly 60,000 adults with type 2 diabetes, those on semaglutide — the drug behind Ozempic and Wegovy — broke fewer bones than people on rival weight-loss treatments, easing a long-standing worry that rapid weight loss leaves the skeleton fragile.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A study of nearly 60,000 diabetes patients found semaglutide users had a lower fracture rate than those on rival weight-loss drugs
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indians carry one of the world's heaviest burdens of type 2 diabetes and are increasingly being prescribed GLP-1 drugs in India and abroad — so reassurance that semaglutide does not appear to crumble the bones of diabetic patients, and may even guard them, speaks directly to millions of NRI families weighing whether a parent or partner should start one of these medicines.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: A Common Vitamin in Citrus and Greens Is Linked to a Better-Preserved Brain in Older Age
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In more than 2,000 older adults, those with higher blood levels of vitamin C had more grey matter and stronger memory-network connections on brain scans — the first study to tie measured vitamin C, not just diet surveys, to the brain's structure.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Citrus, amla, tomatoes and leafy greens are among the richest dietary sources of vitamin C, linked to better-preserved brain structure
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Indian cuisine is rich in the very foods that deliver vitamin C — amla, citrus, guava, tomatoes, green chillies and leafy saag — yet long cooking and changing diets can strip it away, making this a timely, low-cost reminder for diaspora families that protecting an ageing parent's mind may start with what is on the plate.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: One of the Biggest Risks for Dementia Is Also One of the Easiest to Treat — and It Sits in the Ears
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A new analysis of more than 16,000 American adults found severe hearing loss was associated with a sharply higher risk of dementia, while a major randomized trial showed that simply fitting at-risk elders with hearing aids slowed their cognitive decline by nearly half.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Researchers found fitting at-risk older adults with hearing aids cut their rate of cognitive decline by nearly half
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: In many Indian families, an elder's fading hearing is quietly accepted as a normal part of getting old and rarely treated — yet this research reframes an untreated hearing problem as a serious, fixable threat to the mind, making a hearing test and a pair of hearing aids one of the most worthwhile gifts an NRI child can arrange for a parent ageing in India or abroad.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: Scientists Have Found Microplastics Inside the Human Eye — and the More There Were, the Higher the Pressure
lifestyle-health.excerpt: In the first study to look, researchers detected microplastic particles in every sample of a delicate drainage tissue taken from glaucoma patients, and the plastic burden tracked closely with the dangerously high eye pressure that drives the disease.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: Scientists detected microplastic particles in the eye's fluid-draining tissue, linked to higher intraocular pressure in glaucoma patients
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: Glaucoma is a leading cause of irreversible blindness in India, and the diaspora hails from some of the most plastic-saturated, air-polluted cities on earth — so early evidence that plastic particles may lodge in the eye and push up the pressure that steals sight is a story that lands close to home for millions of NRI families.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: The Weakness That Comes With Age May Live as Much in the Brain as in the Muscle, a New Study Finds
lifestyle-health.excerpt: When researchers gave older adults a jolt of electrical stimulation at the moment they thought they were pushing as hard as they could, the weakest among them produced far more force — a sign that ageing nerves, not just shrinking muscle, may be holding strength back.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A study of 66 older adults found weaker participants had untapped muscle strength their nervous systems were not fully activating
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: For NRI families caring for ageing parents across continents — often advising on health by video call — the finding reframes the goal from simply lifting weights to keeping the brain-to-muscle connection sharp, suggesting that balance work, coordination and learning new movements deserve a place alongside resistance training in the routines that keep elders independent.
lifestyle-health.author: Diaspora Desk

lifestyle-health.title: People on Ozempic-Style Drugs Are Moving Less, Not More — and Doctors Say That Undercuts the Benefit
lifestyle-health.excerpt: A study of 753 adults using fitness-tracker data found that daily steps and exercise actually fell after people started GLP-1 weight-loss medications, raising the risk that muscle is lost along with fat unless physical activity is built in deliberately.
lifestyle-health.image_caption: A study of 753 adults found daily steps and exercise fell after people began GLP-1 weight-loss medications
lifestyle-health.nri_angle: GLP-1 drugs have spread fast among diaspora Indians battling the high rates of diabetes and obesity that run in South Asian families, and this finding is a pointed warning — for a group already prone to losing muscle and storing dangerous fat, taking the medication without keeping up movement risks trading one health problem for another.
